problem_class.label: convex
problem_class.details: Minimize F(x)=max_{i<m} loss_i(x) over the closed Euclidean ball B(x0,R). Every component is convex on this ball; a constrained minimizer exists.

oracle.label: component_gradient
oracle.details: A query (i,x) returns the exact gradient of component i for every in-domain x, independently of history and oracle seed.

oracle.label: function_value
oracle.details: The same query also returns the exact component value loss_i(x); the value-gradient pair counts as one oracle call.
oracle.evidence: LongTails/Setups/SmoothFiniteMaximum.lean: spec.Reply and spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: executeWithTrace and _run.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Public parameters include m≥2, G>0, L≥0, R>0, ε>0, δ∈(0,1), and x0. On B(x0,R), each component satisfies ||∇loss_i(x)||≤G and ||∇loss_i(x)−∇loss_i(y)||≤L||x−y||. Component functions and the constrained minimizer are hidden. No oracle error is permitted on the domain.

accuracy.label: objective_gap
accuracy.details: The measurable output x must satisfy F(x)−F(xstar)≤ε on the success event.

accuracy.label: almost_sure
accuracy.details: The output belongs to B(x0,R) almost surely; this guarantee concerns feasibility.

accuracy.label: high_probability
accuracy.details: The objective-gap event has probability at least 1−δ under the joint algorithm and oracle seed law, with a fixed oracle budget.

setup_category.label: classical
setup_category.reason: Constrained minimization of a finite maximum of convex smooth Lipschitz components using exact component first-order queries is an established optimization formulation.

descriptionHtml:
Smooth Finite-Maximum Minimization

We minimize F(x)=max1≤i≤mfi(x) over C={x∈E:∥x−x0∥≤R}, where E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, x0∈E, R>0, and m≥2 is an integer. Each fi:E→R is convex on C, differentiable at every point of C, and has an L-Lipschitz gradient bounded in norm by G, where L≥0 and G>0. The oracle returns (fi(x),∇fi(x)) at (i,x) with x∈C. Given ε>0 and δ∈(0,1), the goal is a measurable output x¯∈C almost surely satisfying F(x¯)−F(x⋆)≤ε with probability at least 1−δ, where x⋆ minimizes F on C and probabilities follow the law P of the algorithm’s randomness.

The optimization problem is minx∈CF(x). The norm ∥⋅∥ is induced by the inner product on E. The algorithm receives E, m, G, L, R, ε, δ, and x0; the component functions and the minimizer are accessed only through the specified oracle information.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Component convexity). For every i∈{1,…,m}, x,y∈C, and t∈[0,1], fi((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)fi(x)+tfi(y).

Assumption 2 (Component regularity). Each fi:E→R is Fréchet differentiable at every x∈C. For every i∈{1,…,m} and x,y∈C, ∥∇fi(x)∥≤G,∥∇fi(x)−∇fi(y)∥≤L∥x−y∥.

Assumption 3 (Constrained minimizer). There exists x⋆∈C such that F(x⋆)≤F(x),x∈C.

Oracle access consists of component queries: choosing an index i∈{1,…,m} and a point x∈C returns the exact value and gradient of that component. Each such pair is obtained in one oracle call.

After the allotted calls, the output x¯ must be measurable and satisfy x¯∈CP-a.s.,P(F(x¯)−F(x⋆)≤ε)≥1−δ.

comparisonHtml:
In a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, minimize F(x)=maxi≤mfi(x) over B=B―(x0,R), with m≥2. Each fi is convex and differentiable on B, with ∥∇fi∥≤G and L-Lipschitz gradient there; a constrained minimizer x⋆∈B exists. Here G,R,ε>0, L≥0, and 0<δ<1. One exact component query returns (fi(x),∇fi(x)). The target is a measurable feasible output x^ with Pr{F(x^)−F(x⋆)≤ε}≥1−δ.

Comparison for SmoothFiniteMaximum.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) AffineSoftmaxFiniteMaximum (Ours) (⋆⋆⋆) (review) O(hℓ7[m+mt1/3+m3/4t1/2+m6/7(st)2/7+s]); deterministic query cap.
(2) Accelerated linearization (Carmon et al. 2021), App. A.3 O(m(1+t)); deterministic accuracy. (1): Rate, normalized regime: polynomial saving for m≫ε−1/2. At m=ε−3/2, O(ε−2) becomes O(hℓ7ε−13/7). (1): Worse for m≪ε−1/2 in the normalized regime; randomized, with hℓ7 overhead and a much larger universal constant.
(3) (Carmon et al. 2023), Thm. 8.1, ball case; confidence amplification O(h[mt1/3+s2]polylog(2+m+s+t)), for 0<ε≤min{LR2,G2/L}. Includes repetitions and O(mh) scoring queries. (1): Rate, normalized regime: polynomial saving for m≪ε−5/3 within the stated accuracy range; matches polynomial order for m≳ε−5/3. Drops the accuracy restriction. (1): Larger polylogarithms and universal constant; query guarantee only, versus runtime bounds and an additional simplex setting.
(4) (Carmon et al. 2021), Thm. 2; unconstrained, globally convex, G-Lipschitz, L-smooth components; global minimizer within R of x0 O(hk3[m{1+(slog⁡m)2/3}+m(slog⁡m+t)]); includes confidence amplification and scoring. (1): On common global-minimizer instances, polynomial saving for every m=ε−α, α>0, in the normalized regime. Scope: local ball assumptions suffice; classes overlap, without nesting. (1): Can lose when L≫G2/ε. For G=R=1, L=ε−2: contains mε−1 versus mε−2/3+mε−3/2, ignoring logarithms.

Abbr: s=GR/ε, t=LR2/ε, h=1+log⁡(1/δ), ℓ=log⁡(2+m+s+t), k=1+log⁡(1+slog⁡m). polylog(u) denotes the source’s unspecified polynomial in 1+log⁡u. Normalized regime: G=L=R=1, ε↓0; polynomial comparisons ignore logarithmic factors and use fixed confidence.

source:
import LongTails.Template
import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.Gradient.Basic
import Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Function
import Mathlib.Analysis.Normed.Module.FiniteDimension
import Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Constructions.BorelSpace.Basic

open Set MeasureTheory

namespace LongTails.Setups.SmoothFiniteMaximum

open OracleTemplate

structure Public where
  E : Type
  [normedE : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [innerE : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [finiteE : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [measurableE : MeasurableSpace E]
  [borelE : BorelSpace E]
  m : ℕ
  hm : 2 ≤ m
  G : ℝ
  L : ℝ
  R : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  δ : ℝ
  x0 : E

attribute [instance] Public.normedE Public.innerE Public.finiteE
  Public.measurableE Public.borelE

def domain (p : Public) : Set p.E := Metric.closedBall p.x0 p.R

structure Instance (p : Public) where
  loss : Fin p.m → p.E → ℝ
  xstar : p.E

noncomputable def objective {p : Public} (I : Instance p) (x : p.E) : ℝ :=
  sSup (Set.range fun i => I.loss i x)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Public
  Public := Public
  Instance := Instance
  Query p := Fin p.m × p.E
  Reply p := ℝ × p.E
  Output p := p.E
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.G ∧ 0 ≤ p.L ∧ 0 < p.R ∧ 0 < p.ε ∧ 0 < p.δ ∧ p.δ < 1
  admissible p I oracle :=
    (∀ i, ConvexOn ℝ (domain p) (I.loss i)) ∧
    (∀ i x, x ∈ domain p → HasGradientAt (I.loss i) (gradient (I.loss i) x) x) ∧
    (∀ i x, x ∈ domain p → ‖gradient (I.loss i) x‖ ≤ p.G) ∧
    (∀ i x y, x ∈ domain p → y ∈ domain p →
      ‖gradient (I.loss i) x - gradient (I.loss i) y‖ ≤ p.L * ‖x - y‖) ∧
    I.xstar ∈ domain p ∧ IsMinOn (objective I) (domain p) I.xstar ∧
    (∀ history seed i x, x ∈ domain p →
      oracle.answer history (0, (i, x)) seed = (I.loss i x, gradient (I.loss i) x))
  successful p I output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
    (∀ᵐ ω ∂(P : Measure _), output ω ∈ domain p) ∧
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 - p.δ) ≤
      (P : Measure _) {ω | objective I (output ω) - objective I I.xstar ≤ p.ε}

end LongTails.Setups.SmoothFiniteMaximum
